  "reasoning": "The BOOK ENTRY's core identification—that gnashing of teeth depicts the rage and hatred of the excluded wicked directed at the righteous when they see the kingdom—aligns precisely with the supplied scriptural evidence and the chapter's demonstration. The chapter establishes that the Hebrew root charaq consistently denotes hostility toward the righteous across Psalms, Job, Lamentations, and Acts 7:54, never pain or torment. Luke 13:28's ʻsee the kingdom and be thrust outʼ directly parallels Psalm 112:10's ʻsee it, be grieved, gnash, and melt awayʼ, confirming the scene as grief-plus-rage culminating in destruction rather than endless conscious suffering. The entry's emphasis on the pattern of Psalms and Stephen's acc users is fully supported by these texts and the chapter's cross-references.

  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The entry's core is fixed by the exact verbal and scenic match of Luke 13:28 to Psalm 112:10 (see the blessed/kingdom, grieve, gnash, then perish/melt) together with the uniform OT/Acts usage of gnashing as hostile rage of the wicked at the righteous (Ps 37:12; Acts 7:54). That pattern accounts for the fixed Synoptic formula better than a generic 'anguish of the damned' reading, which must treat the OT parallels as irrelevant or metaphorical and cannot explain why the texts repeatedly stage the gnashing as a reaction to seeing the righteous inside. Secondary wording in the entry (grief + hatred + destruction following the Psalms/Stephen pattern) is likewise carried by the same texts. No material assertion printed in the entry itself is left unsupported; broader chapter claims about Sheol vocabulary or non-repentance are out of glossary scope.",
  "book_core_identification": "Gnashing of teeth is the rage/hatred of the wicked directed at the righteous, especially when the wicked see the kingdom from which they themselves are excluded.",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Their grief, hatred, gnashing, and destruction follow the pattern of the Psalms and Stephen's accusers."
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Chapter claim that every Matthean 'outer darkness'/furnace destination is simply the vocabulary of the grave/Sheol/Gehinnom and therefore proves melting-away rather than ongoing torment.",
    "Chapter claim that the definite articles plus Hebrew Matthew charaq make the formula a rigid quotation of Psalm 112 rather than a stock apocalyptic idiom.",
    "Chapter claim that the gnashing itself functions as courtroom evidence that the excluded remain unrepentant."
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "In the Synoptic judgment sayings the fixed phrase 'weeping and gnashing of teeth' is stock imagery for the extreme anguish, despair and remorse of those finally excluded from the kingdom and consigned to eschatological punishment (outer darkness, furnace), without requiring that the dominant emotion be hostile rage at the righteous or that the scene be a direct reuse of Psalm 112.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Extreme anguish/despair/remorse of the condemned at final exclusion and punishment.",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter denies that the primary and defining referent of the gnashing is rage directed at the righteous (upon seeing them in the kingdom); it treats that emotion, if present at all, as secondary to self-focused suffering.",

    "The seven Synoptic occurrences are all embedded in scenes of judgment, expulsion, darkness or fire, which naturally suggest the misery of the punished rather than a specific hostile glare at the blessed.",

    "Later Christian tradition and many modern commentaries have consistently heard the phrase as describing the conscious suffering of the damned."
  ],

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
